_comment: Phase 5 animated tiles. Tile id -> how that tile moves. Levels never mention this: the renderer looks every drawn tile up here, so adding an entry animates every existing level at once. Ids match data/tiles.json and are never changed by animation - collision reads the id, not the frame.

_effects.frames: indices into the fx atlas above, cycled at 'fps'
_effects.sway: draw offset in px along 'axis'; 'row_phase' staggers successive tile rows so foliage ripples instead of sliding as one sheet
_effects.tint: brightness multiplier swinging +/- 'amount' at 'hz' - a light source that breathes

7.name: water_top
7._note: Phase C, docs/plan-art-motion.md: frames 8-11 are a sparkle+foam phase of the SAME wave (tools/gen_fx.py::water_sparkle_frame), not a second tile -- 'if a new tile id would be needed, do NOT add one' ruled out a shoreline-foam variant tile outright, so foam is four more frames on water_top instead. The 8-frame cycle alternates plain crest (0-3) with the glinting one (8-11), which is what makes a long run of water_top shimmer rather than just scroll.

206.name: updraft
206._note: THE UPDRAFT. World 3's core verb, and until now the only thing in the game that moved the player while standing perfectly still itself. A sway on the y axis with a row phase is a travelling wave rather than a bob: hold the phase constant and ty falls as t rises, so the ripple runs UP the column, which is the direction the tile pushes. 0.34 puts roughly three rows in a wavelength - a column four tiles tall shows a whole crest, which is the shortest one that is authored.

207.name: updraft_strong
207._note: updraft_strong, [0,-560] against the updraft's [0,-400]. Faster and one row shorter in the wave, so the two columns read as different strengths from across a screen without either of them needing its own artwork. Still 1 px: the cap is 2 and 2 px of vertical slide tears a streak away from the one above it.

248.name: heights_chain
248._note: heights_chain. A hang sway like the vine's, slower and with less phase between rows: a chain is stiffer than a creeper, so it swings closer to one piece.

250.name: heights_cloud
250._note: heights_cloud. The slowest thing in the table - half the rate of the jungle's bg_leaves, which is itself the slow one. It is a background fill rather than a prop, so the drift has to be under the threshold where the eye starts reading the tile grid instead of the weather.

267.name: deep_spore
267._note: deep_spore. World 4's hazard, and the first one in this table that is lit from inside rather than on fire - data/ambience.json gives 267 an emissive pool in THE LIGHTLESS, because a dark hazard you cannot see is not a lesson, it is a coin toss. So it breathes rather than moves: a tint and not a sway, because a hazard that slides a pixel sideways is a hazard whose edge lies about where it is, and the whole point of the spore pit is that you see it coming. 0.10 at 0.42 Hz is a two-and-a-half second breath - an eighth of the lava's rate and well under its amount, which is the difference between a spore mat exhaling and something burning.

281.name: obsidian_hot
281._note: Phase C, docs/plan-art-motion.md: world 5's turn at the M4-established tint pattern (267's spore breath, 24's lava pulse) -- the one hazard tile the M4/M5 passes left un-animated. obsidian_hot is molten glass under a crust, not an open flame and not a lightless hazard either, so its pulse sits between the two it is modelled on: faster than the spore's 0.42 Hz (this is actively hot, not a slow exhale) but nowhere near the lava's 3.1 Hz (it is glass over the heat, not the heat itself) and held to 0.12 amount, under spore's headroom and well under lava's 0.16, so a whole wall of it breathes without burning through data/ambience.json's own emissive pool on the same tile.
